Prospective Students & Applicants
The Application Cycle for the PhD Program for Fall 2027 Enrollment is OPEN.
The Application Cycle for the MS Program for Fall 2027 Enrollment is OPEN.
Please take a moment to learn about the Georgetown University Graduate Program in Physics by viewing our Webinar Recording Below:
Video link:
https://youtu.be/gJylHyugKEE
Graduate Program in Physics Webinar (December 2020)
Application Process and Requirements
Our application deadline for the PhD Program is January 15th.
The application deadline for the MS Program is May 1st.
All applications to the Graduate Physics Program should be submitted electronically through the Georgetown University Office of Graduate Admissions application portal
The Office of Graduate Studies Physics page includes the most current information on deadlines and requirements.
Note: The Office of Graduate Admissions will not accept any credentials via email or fax.
Application Requirements:
Important notice regarding the General and Physics GRE requirement for the 2026-2027 application cycle
GRE scores will NOT be required this year, and their absence will not be used to count against any applicant.
A completed application consists of (1) an online application form (application portal), (2) an application fee ($90), and the following credentials:
Graduate Record Exam (GRE) General test: (waived for the 2026-2027 admission cycle)
GRE Physics Subject test: (waived for the 2026-2027 admission cycle)
Transcripts – Applicants are required to upload to the application system copies of official transcripts from all undergraduate and graduate institutions attended. Visit our How to Apply (new window) page for additional details and FAQs.
Resume or curriculum vitae (CV)
3 letters of recommendation
Academic statement of purpose
TOEFL or IELTS score
Our Requirements
Achieve a Bachelor’s degree in Physics or a related field
Maintain a minimum GPA of 3.0 in an accredited undergraduate program
Take the GRE (waived for the 2026-2027 admission cycle)
Take the Physics Subject GRE (waived for the 2026-2027 admission cycle)
Score a minimum of 100 (original TOEFL iBT score scale) or 5 (new TOEFL iBT score scale beginning January 21, 2026) on the TOEFL exam or 7.5 on the IELTS exam**
For applicants from non-English speaking countries only​
Note: TOEFL and IELTS scores are valid for 2 years from the date of the test.
**Duolingo English Test: Georgetown University has discontinued the use of the Duolingo English Test for Graduate Admissions, effective July 2021
Statement of Purpose
The statement of purpose should be one to two pages long. It should describe your background as it relates to your interest in pursuing graduate studies in the physics program at Georgetown. For example, you could mention academics, research and work experience, and community contributions. Your statement should also cover your academic and professional goals, how the physics program will help you achieve those goals, your talents and abilities, and the reason why you want to pursue an advanced degree. If your academic record has areas of concern, please address them here.
Optional
If you are interested in being considered for the GU IMSD program, please discuss in a few sentences why you are interested in the IMSD program and what you hope to both gain from and contribute to the program. Ph.D. program directors will nominate IMSD fellows for consideration. Interviews for the IMSD will take place in the late winter/early spring.
For more information, please see the Graduate Fellowship section.
Letters of Recommendation
It is important to carefully select the people who will write your letters of recommendation; grades and scores do not reflect the totality of the applicant. Choose individuals who will accurately assess your capacity for research and have known you for an extended period, such as your academic Advisor or Research Mentor. Recommendation letters should directly address your preparedness for graduate studies in physics and should attest to your research experience and potential for success at Georgetown.
International Students
For applicants whose native language is not English, certification of English language proficiency is required via TOEFL or IELTS.
The minimum TOEFL score is 100 (original TOEFL iBT score scale) or 5 (new TOEFL iBT score scale beginning January 21, 2026)
The minimum IELTS score is 7.5.
Note: these requirements are stricter than those of the University Office of Graduate Studies.
Transfer Students
We welcome applications for the Ph.D. degree from students who already hold Master’s degrees. Applications from transfer students will be determined on a case-by-case basis.
Application Fee Waiver Requests
Application Fee Waiver Requests are now processed directly via the application portal. Applicants who meet one or more of the listed eligibility criteria may request a fee waiver in the Application Fee Waiver section of the application. Some fee waivers may require additional information or documentation.
Feel free to contact us with your questions at graduatehelp@physics.georgetown.edu or sign up through our Inquiry Form to receive additional information regarding our Graduate Program!
